what: Within-template control for the RQ3 granularity claim. On SCP the injected-span length and the template are nearly collinear (scp_z injects 2-6 words, scp_p 7-14, scp_i 94-216), so the pooled bucket comparison cannot separate 'the fine cut resolves short payloads' from 'the fine cut suits one template'. Holding the template fixed and varying only length separates them.

verdict.key_evidence: Within scp_z alone -- one template, one construction -- count:6/runs blocks 0.8584 on 1-2-word injections (n=113) and 0.9412 on 3-4-word ones (n=136), a 8.3pp swing driven by length only, while width:2:cap16/runs moves 0.9469 -> 0.9632 (1.6pp). The coarse cut is length-sensitive and the fine cut is nearly not, which is the mechanism the deployed union assumes.
verdict.long_end: The both-extremes finding also survives: within scp_p, count:6/runs falls 0.9727 (5-8, n=220) -> 0.9556 (9-16, n=45) while width:2 rises to 1.000.
verdict.caveat: scp_z's 5-8 bucket is n=18 and scp_p's 9-16 is n=45; the well-powered comparison is scp_z 1-2 vs 3-4 (n=113 vs 136). scp_i occupies a single bucket (17+), so it contributes no within-template length contrast.
